svg.text: Entity Extraction & Knowledge Graph Construction (One-Time — Most Expensive Indexing In The Repo)
📌 SUMMARY: Every chunk costs one LLM extraction call. Typed entities become graph nodes,
relationships become weighted edges — both remember their source chunk ids. Louvain communities
are tagged on. A vector index is built alongside purely for query-time backfill.
💡 Priced in LLM calls: chunks × 1 — budget accordingly

g.text: nodes = typed entities · edges = weighted relations
every node/edge stores its source chunk_ids

svg.text: Match Entities → Traverse Graph → Assemble Context → Backfill → Generate (Per Query)
📌 SUMMARY: One entity-extraction call per query, then the answer path is a graph walk.
Chunks are chosen because matched entities REFERENCE them — not because embeddings look similar.
Short or unmatched queries degrade honestly to dense retrieval and say so in metadata.
① MATCH — Question Entities vs. Graph Nodes
💡 Which path fired is reported as context_source metadata
② TRAVERSE & ASSEMBLE — Context From Connections
💡 Hub entities can reference dozens of chunks — the cap keeps prompts bounded
💡 Backfill reuses the offline vector index; duplicates removed by content prefix
💡 Result reports graph_chunks and dense_backfilled counts separately
③ GENERATE — Synthesize Across Entity Facts
💡 Multi-hop questions get real relation paths, not embedding luck
💡 Every result is auditable: which entities matched, where context came from
